`JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(value))` turns a `Date` into a string, drops `undefined`, turns a `Map` or `Set` into `{}`, and throws on an object that refers to itself. `structuredClone()` is built in and copies all of these correctly, so a library function such as lodash's `cloneDeep` is not needed either.

## Examples

Reported:

{/* bad {"count": 2} */}
```js
const draft = JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(settings));
const backup = _.cloneDeep(settings);
```

Not reported:

{/* good */}
```js
const draft = structuredClone(settings);
```

## Options

| Option | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `functions` | `["cloneDeep", "utils.clone"]` | Names of functions to report. The list replaces the default. |

A name with a dot, such as `utils.clone`, matches only that object and method. A name without a dot matches a call of that function and a method of that name on any object.

{/* bad {"options": [{"functions": ["deepCopy"]}]} */}
```js
const draft = deepCopy(settings);
```

{/* good {"options": [{"functions": ["deepCopy"]}]} */}
```js
const backup = _.cloneDeep(settings);
```

## When not to use it

`structuredClone()` throws on functions and DOM nodes, and the copy of a class instance is a plain object. If you clone such values, keep your own function.
